quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When getting ready to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: Right
Center
Left

questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely need to:

options.text: Reduce the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure adjustments.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires before riding. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure settings.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to proceed.
You should continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road while avoiding another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve or turn. This can cause a motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: How should you position your body on the motorcycle?

options.text: You should hold yourself up with your arms.
Your arms should be used to steer the motorcycle.
You should have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your arms should be used to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Sit so your elbows are slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When carrying a load, where should it be secured?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Secure loads low to keep the motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will enter the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means they see you.
Doesn't mean they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume a driver will yield just because you made eye contact. A driver may look directly at a motorcyclist and still not see them.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
The driver usually cannot see you.
This position should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position increases your visibility.

questions.question: When carrying a load, where should it be secured?

options.text: As low as possible.
As high as possible.
To a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Loads should be secured as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely and wait until the train has passed and the lights stop flashing. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do about the speed limit?

options.text: You may go 10 mph over the limit.
You must not exceed the speed limit.
You must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete passing within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What usually causes a wobble (shaking of the front wheel and handlebars)?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
The front wheel not being tightened properly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is caused mostly by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle respond to turns?

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight. The motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn because of this added weight.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra careful at intersections.

questions.question: How should you stay safe on a long trip?

options.text: Ride as far as you can in one day.
Stop as little as possible.
Do not use artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: Avoid artificial stimulants because they can cause extreme fatigue when they wear off. Limit riding to about six hours per day and take a rest break every two hours.

questions.question: What formation is best for group riding while keeping safe distance?

options.text: Single-file.
Riding in pairs.
Staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation allows riders to stay together while each rider has adequate space cushion.

questions.question: What should you do if the front wheel locks while braking?

options.text: Release the front brake, then re-apply it.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake, then re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake right away and re-apply it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the animal loses interest.
Slow down, then quickly speed up and ride away as the dog approaches.
Swerve around the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, then quickly speed up and ride away as the dog approaches.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches your motorcycle, slow down and downshift as it gets close. Then quickly accelerate away from the animal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for an area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They make objects look farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: Why is it a problem for a motorcyclist to ride next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see the motorcyclist.
The motorcyclist may not see road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could swerve into your lane. It could also block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders can make you steer off course.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need?

options.text: Less room to stop than larger vehicles.
As much room to stop as larger vehicles.
Can stop instantly.

questions.correctAnswerText: As much room to stop as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always keep enough space to stop safely. Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as other vehicles.

questions.question: When should you wear hearing protection?

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Only recommended for long trips.
On all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection every time you ride.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
questions.explanation: Before riding, tell your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction of turns or curves. This helps you and your bike lean the right way.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to improve your view.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.
